mainTopic: Whether tree roots follow the tree or the land, the sixteen-אמה rule, and עולא's source for it.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע defended cutting רב פפא's palm roots by quoting רב יהודה's rule about a public strip. Afterward he realized he could simply have said he cut beyond sixteen אמות. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: someone digging a pit may cut roots, 'and the wood is his.' יעקב הדייבא asks whose wood that is. רב חסדא tries to prove from a משנה in מעילה that roots follow the tree. The proof is challenged from the second half of that משנה. One answer says the משנה is about new growths and proves nothing. רבינא answers instead that it depends on whether the roots are within or beyond sixteen אמות. Finally, עולא rules that a tree within sixteen אמות of a border is a גזלן and cannot be used for ביכורים. The גמרא searches for his source in the משנה of שביעית, and that search continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Winning the argument with רב יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע tells how he ended the argument with רב פפא: he quoted רב יהודה's rule that a strip the public has used may not be ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until I told him what רב יהודה said: a border strip that the public has acquired a right to use may not be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a story. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the argument with רב פפא stopped once he quoted רב יהודה's rule about a public strip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה says that once people have an established right to use a strip of land, nobody may ruin it. רב הונא used this to defend his own established use of his land, so רב פפא could not stop his digging.

keyTerms.meaning: A border strip or boundary path between fields
The public has gained an established right to use it
It is forbidden to ruin it

phrases.english: until I told him
that which Rav Yehuda said:
a border strip that the public has acquired a right to use
it is forbidden to ruin it.
phrases.notes: He applied this to himself: since he already had a right to use his land, it could not be taken from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד דַּאֲמַרִי לֵיהּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun earlier on the דף.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's right to keep digging and cutting the roots
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה: מצר שהחזיקו בו רבים אסור לקלקלו

steps.title: A better answer he thought of later: the sixteen-אמה line
steps.stepSummary: After רב פפא left, רב הונא realized he could have given a stronger answer: roots count as part of the tree only within sixteen אמות, and he had cut them beyond that.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he left, I said: Why didn't I tell him that there the rule applies within sixteen אמות, and here I was cutting beyond sixteen אמות?
steps.whatsHappening: After the conversation ended, רב הונא thought of a cleaner answer he wished he had given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within sixteen אמות of a tree, the roots still count as part of the tree, so the tree owner has a claim there. Beyond sixteen אמות they do not. Since he cut beyond that line, רב פפא had no claim at all, and he did not even need רב יהודה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: After he left
Sixteen אמות, the distance within which roots count as part of the tree
Here... there; used to split two cases

phrases.english: After he left, he said:
Why did I not say to him:
there, it is within sixteen cubits,
here, it is beyond sixteen cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר דִּנְפַק, אֲמַר: אַמַּאי לָא אֲמַרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a better defense than the one used in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases by distance from the tree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He needed רב יהודה's rule about established use to defend his digging.
steps.terutzMaskana: Beyond sixteen אמות the roots do not belong to the tree owner, so cutting them is simply allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Roots within sixteen אמות count as part of the tree. Beyond that, they do not.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: digging a pit and cutting roots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone digging a pit, ditch or cave may cut the roots down, and 'the wood is his.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was digging a pit, a ditch or a cave, he may cut downward, and the wood is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next question by quoting the משנה's words about the wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the landowner cut roots that get in the way of his digging. But 'the wood is his' does not say whose wood it is, and that gap leads to the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit, a ditch and a cave: different kinds of digging
He cuts as he goes down
The wood is his

phrases.english: If he was digging a pit, a ditch, or a cave
he may cut downward
and the wood is his (etc.).
phrases.notes: 'His' could mean the tree's owner or the landowner. That's exactly what the next question asks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person digging may cut intruding roots, and the wood is 'his.'

steps.title: Whose wood is it?
steps.stepSummary: יעקב הדייבא asks רב חסדא whether 'his' means the tree owner or the landowner.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב הדייבא asked רב חסדא: Whose is the wood?
steps.whatsHappening: A sage asks a simple clarifying question about the משנה's unclear word 'his.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is really whether roots follow the tree they grow from or the land they grow in. The answer decides who owns the cut wood.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question)
יעקב from הדייב, the sage asking
Whose is the wood?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ יַעֲקֹב הַדְיָיבָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Ya'akov of Hadeyyav asked Rav Ḥisda:
Whose is the wood?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ יַעֲקֹב הַדְיָיבָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear wording in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'his' mean the tree owner or the landowner? In other words, do roots follow the tree or the land?

steps.title: רב חסדא: you already learned it, roots of a private tree in הקדש land
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes a משנה: roots of a private person's tree that reach into הקדש land may not be used, but using them is not מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it already. Roots of a private person's tree that reach into הקדש land may not be used for benefit, but one who uses them does not commit מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by pointing to a משנה the questioner already knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roots belong to a private tree but sit in הקדש land. The משנה rules that benefit is forbidden, yet there is no מעילה, so the roots are not treated as fully holy. The next step explains why this answers the question.

keyTerms.meaning: You have learned it already
An ordinary private person, not the בית המקדש
Property belonging to the בית המקדש
Committing מעילה, the misuse of holy property that requires a קרבן

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
phrases.notes: This comes from a משנה in מסכת מעילה.

phrases.english: Roots of a tree belonging to an ordinary person
that extend into land belonging to the Temple,
one may not benefit from them, but one is not liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4 by citing a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה about private roots in הקדש land shows how roots are treated.

steps.title: Why the משנה proves roots follow the tree
steps.stepSummary: No מעילה makes sense only if roots follow the tree, which is private. If they followed the land, which is הקדש, there should be מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say we follow the tree; that is why there is no מעילה. But if you say we follow the land, why is there no מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא spells out the proof: the משנה's ruling fits only the view that roots belong with the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If roots belonged to the land, these roots would be הקדש, and using them would be מעילה. Since the משנה says there is no מעילה, the roots must follow the private tree. By this proof, 'the wood is his' in our משנה would mean the tree owner's, but the next steps question it.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say...
We follow the tree
We follow the land

phrases.english: Granted, if you say:
we follow the tree
that is why one is not liable for misuse;
but if you say:
we follow the land,
why is one not liable for misuse?
phrases.notes: If the land rule were true, the roots would be holy like the הקדש land, so there should be מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא: בָּתַר אִילָן אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 5 answers the question.
steps.raayaObject: Roots follow the tree, so the cut wood belongs to the tree owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעילה: private roots in הקדש land, with no מעילה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's proof: no מעילה on private roots in הקדש land suggests that roots follow the tree, not the land. Step 7 challenges this proof. Step 8 shows the משנה may prove nothing about roots, and in step 9 רבינא makes it depend on distance.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No מעילה' does not mean using the roots is allowed. Benefit is still forbidden (לא נהנין). The only point is that the roots are not fully הקדש.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה seems to say roots follow the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 6. In the סיפא, roots of a הקדש tree that reach into a private field carry no מעילה. If roots followed the tree, they would be הקדש and there should be מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, do we follow the tree? Look at the end of that משנה: if roots of a הקדש tree reach into a private person's field, you may not use them, but there is no מעילה. If roots follow the tree, why is there no מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof that roots follow the tree. It points to the very next line of the same משנה, which seems to show the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said: private tree, roots in הקדש land, no מעילה, so roots follow the tree. But the סיפא is the reverse case: the tree is הקדש and the land is private, and there is still no מעילה. If roots followed the tree, these roots would be הקדש and using them should be מעילה, so the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what?' A phrase that opens a challenge to the position just taken
We follow the tree, meaning roots are treated as part of the tree
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Property that belongs to the בית המקדש
An ordinary private person, as opposed to הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Both halves of the משנה end with 'no מעילה,' but the cases are reversed. In the רישא the tree is private and the land is הקדש. In the סיפא the tree is הקדש and the land is private.

phrases.english: Rather, what? Do we follow the tree?!
Say the last clause:
Roots of a הקדש tree that come into a private person's field,
one may not benefit from them, but one does not commit מעילה.
And if we follow the tree,
why is there no מעילה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי? בָּתַר אִילָן אָזְלִינַן?! אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in step 6 using the second half of the same משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 6 that roots follow the tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If roots follow the tree, roots of a הקדש tree should be הקדש, so using them should be מעילה. The סיפא says there is no מעילה, which suggests roots follow the private land.

steps.title: The משנה is about new growth, so it proves nothing about roots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases are not a real comparison. The whole משנה deals with growth that came after the property became הקדש, and this תנא holds there is no מעילה on new growth. So neither half teaches anything about whether roots follow the tree or the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? We are dealing with growth that came later, and the תנא holds there is no מעילה on new growth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the whole argument from this משנה. It says the 'no מעילה' in the משנה has a different reason that has nothing to do with roots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roots in question grew after the property became הקדש. This תנא holds that later growths never carry מעילה. So 'no מעילה' in both halves comes from that rule, and the משנה is not evidence for either side: not for step 6's proof and not for step 7's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it comparable?' A phrase saying the two cases are not really the same
Growths, new parts that grew later
The sin of using הקדש property for yourself, which requires a קרבן and repayment
We are dealing with (a particular case)

phrases.english: Is it comparable?!
We are dealing with growths that came afterward,
phrases.notes: He means roots that grew after the property became הקדש.

phrases.english: and he holds:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of the משנה.

phrases.english: There is no מעילה with growths.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא?! בְּגִידּוּלִין הַבָּאִין לְאַחַר מִכָּאן עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by showing that the whole משנה, including the proof in step 6, is about something else
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of this משנה as evidence for either side of the roots question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'No מעילה' in the משנה comes from the rule that later growths carry no מעילה, not from whether roots follow the tree or the land
steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, the משנה in מעילה cannot settle יעקב הדייבא's question, because 'no מעילה' comes from the rule about new growth.

steps.title: רבינא: within sixteen אמות versus beyond sixteen אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives another way to resolve the contradiction. The first half of the משנה is about roots within sixteen אמות of the tree, which follow the tree. The second half is about roots beyond sixteen אמות, which follow the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is not difficult. Here it is within sixteen אמות, and there it is beyond sixteen אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer to the challenge in step 7. He explains that the two halves of the משנה describe roots at different distances from the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within sixteen אמות, roots count as part of the tree. So private-tree roots in הקדש land stay private, and there is no מעילה. Beyond sixteen אמות, roots count as part of the land. So הקדש-tree roots in a private field are private, and again there is no מעילה. This uses the same sixteen-אמה line רב הונא used in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The contradiction can be resolved
Here... there. Each source is talking about a different case
Sixteen אמות (cubits), the distance within which roots count as part of the tree

steps.whyThisMatters: According to רבינא, the answer to יעקב הדייבא depends on distance. Within sixteen אמות the roots belong to the tree owner, and beyond that they belong to the landowner.

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is not difficult;
here it is within sixteen cubits,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the first half of the משנה, where the private tree's roots go into הקדש land.

phrases.english: there it is beyond sixteen cubits.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the second half, where the הקדש tree's roots go into a private field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 7, different from step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by distance (כאן... כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the משנה contradict each other about whether roots follow the tree or the land
steps.terutzMaskana: Roots within sixteen אמות follow the tree, and roots beyond sixteen אמות follow the land, so both halves fit together

steps.title: עולא: a tree within sixteen אמות of the border
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that a tree within sixteen אמות of the property line counts as a גזלן, and its owner may not bring ביכורים from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: A tree close to the border, within sixteen אמות, is a robber, and one may not bring ביכורים from it.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a new rule that uses the same sixteen-אמה measure. A tree planted too close to a neighbor's border is treated as stealing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since roots within sixteen אמות count as the tree's own, a tree that close to the border feeds from the neighbor's soil. So its owner is called a גזלן, and fruit from it cannot be brought as ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Border, the property line between fields
Robber, someone who takes what belongs to another
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The sixteen-אמה line keeps coming back. Within it, roots belong to the tree, and a tree that close to a border takes from the neighbor's land.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A tree that is near the border –

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹךְ שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה, גַּזְלָן הוּא –
phrases.english: within sixteen cubits, it is a robber –
phrases.notes: He means the tree draws food from the neighbor's soil, so its owner is treated as taking what isn't his.

phrases.english: and one does not bring first fruits from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement that builds on the sixteen-אמה measure used by רבינא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree within sixteen אמות of a border is considered a גזלן, and ביכורים are not brought from it

steps.title: Where does עולא get sixteen אמות from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of עולא's sixteen-אמות measurement and suggests the משנה about ten saplings in a בית סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does עולא learn this? Perhaps from the משנה that says: if ten saplings are scattered across a בית סאה, one may plow the whole בית סאה for their sake until ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know where עולא's sixteen-אמות number comes from. It offers a first possible source, and the next step will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a tree's roots need a certain amount of ground. The משנה lets you plow a whole field for ten small trees before שביעית, so maybe that field size, split among the trees, tells us how much ground each tree uses. The word אילימא warns us that this suggestion is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? (asking for a source)
If you say (a suggestion that will usually be rejected)
Young saplings
A field area of 50 by 50 אמות
One may plow

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about plowing in the days before שביעית, not about neighbors or ביכורים. The גמרא only wants it for the measurement of how much ground a tree uses.

phrases.english: From where does עולא get this?
If you say it is from what we learned in a משנה:
Ten saplings that are scattered
within a בית סאה,
one may plow the entire בית סאה for their sake,
until ראש השנה.
phrases.notes: This means the ראש השנה that starts the שמיטה year.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לֵיהּ לְעוּלָּא הָא? אִילֵּימָא מִדִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling עולא gave in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the sixteen-אמות measurement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שביעית: ten saplings in a בית סאה

steps.title: The math does not match sixteen אמות
steps.stepSummary: Dividing a בית סאה of 2,500 square אמות among ten saplings gives only 250 square אמות each, which is not עולא's measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: How big is a בית סאה? 2,500 square אמות. How much does each of the ten trees get? 250. That is not עולא's measurement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math and shows the first suggested source cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית סאה is 50 by 50 אמות, so 2,500 square אמות. Ten saplings each get 250 square אמות. Sixteen אמות on every side of a tree is a much bigger area, so this משנה cannot be עולא's source.

keyTerms.meaning: אמות (cubits); here, square אמות
Reaches him; his share
It is not (does not match)

phrases.english: How much is it?
phrases.notes: He means: how big is the area of a בית סאה?

phrases.english: Two thousand five hundred אמות;
For each and every one,
how much does it get?
Two hundred fifty;
This is not עולא's measurement!
phrases.notes: Sixteen אמות on every side is 32 by 32, which is far more than 250.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ten-saplings משנה as the source for עולא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The area per tree (250 square אמות) is much smaller than the area sixteen אמות on each side would cover.

steps.title: A second suggested source: three trees of three people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests instead the משנה about three trees owned by three people that combine, allowing plowing of the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from what we learned: three trees belonging to three people combine, and one may plow the entire (בית סאה for their sake).
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first source, the גמרא offers a different משנה as עולא's source. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the field is shared by only three big trees, not ten saplings, so each tree gets a much bigger share of ground. That bigger share may match עולא's sixteen אמות. The full calculation comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (offering a new answer)
Grown trees
They combine (count together)

phrases.english: But rather, from what we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה אִילָנוֹת שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם –
phrases.english: Three trees belonging to three people,
these combine,
and one may plow the entire

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מִדִּתְנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה אִילָנוֹת שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 12 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא's source may be the משנה about three trees of three people in a בית סאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שביעית: three trees of three people combine
